spec_match.rationale: Runs CSSStyleValue.parse inside a real worker against a regex fallback on the same inputs, which is the feature's actual value proposition, with calc()/scientific-notation/invalid cases showing where the fallback diverges.

interactive.rationale: An editable value list and a Parse button spawn a real blob worker and fill the comparison table; verified the run produced all ten rows with per-row agreement verdicts.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises running both parsers on one list and reading the disagreements, which the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Worker failure and timeout are handled, invalid values (banana, '12 px', unitless 10) are in the default set, and the no-Typed-OM state is explained rather than blank.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5114591051907072 and the Typed OM StyleValue subclasses section.

conformance.rationale: The suite's in-worker parse and conversion assertions cover this page's contract; on Chromium 141 the route honestly reported 2 pass / 5 fail because worker exposure needs Chrome 154.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): clicked Parse — the worker ran, all ten rows rendered with 'rejected (no Typed OM here)' in the Typed OM column and honest regex results beside them; console clean, desktop and mobile screenshots read, no overflow at 360.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits a values-parsed assert with count/hasTypedOm/disagreements.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, agree/differ verdicts as text plus colour, overflow-wrap on cells, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled textarea, captioned table with scoped headers, aria-live result readout, 44px button.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read) — this page's table wraps correctly, unlike its context-probe sibling.

openQuestions.title: Align the no-Typed-OM copy with what the column actually shows
openQuestions.detail: When the worker lacks Typed OM the detail readout says 'its column is empty and only the regex ran', but the Typed OM column is not empty — every row reads 'rejected (no Typed OM here)'. Also the 'agree?' column then marks regex-accepted values as disagreements against a missing API, which is a different kind of 'no' than a real parser disagreement. Reword the fallback detail ('its column reports the missing API') and consider a third verdict state ('not comparable here') so pre-154 visitors do not read API absence as parser disagreement.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/expose-cssstylevalue-hierarchy-to-worker-contexts/parse-in-a-worker/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp), where workers genuinely lack Typed OM. The demo ran a real worker, reported the missing API per row and kept the regex column informative; console/network clean bar the sandbox font-CDN artifact; desktop 1280 and mobile 360 DPR3 screenshots read with no overflow. Feature /conformance/ honestly reported 2 pass / 5 fail on this pre-154 build. One minor copy/verdict-semantics follow-up for the unsupported state.
